generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Unifolium dilatatum: stems 15 cm to 35 cm tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Unifolium dilatatum: leaves 5 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Unifolium dilatatum: leaves 5 cm to 8 cm wide.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Unifolium dilatatum: the flowering stems usually bear 2 leaves; the stem grows in one season.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low herb spreading in carpets, each stem with one or two glossy, heart-shaped leaves and a small spike of white flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.22 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy bright green leaves; white flowers.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescences racemose, complex, 15 to 40 flowered, the flowers (1 to) 3 (to 4) at a node, their parts in twos. The Flora of North America's account of the species, with Jepson eFlora and the Burke Herbarium, as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read: flowers 2-merous, with 4 distinct white tepals about 2.5 mm long, reflexed to spreading, and 4 stamens at their bases; a Puget Sound field-botany page adds a 2-parted ovary, so 2 carpels (the genus has 2 or 3).

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its raceme drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind and its flowers from its characters, by the rules at the flowering plants; three flowers at each node, each a white star of four tepals about 5 mm across (tepals 2 to 3.2 mm in the Flora of North America), on short pedicels. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four white tepals in two pairs, four stamens and a two-carpelled pistil, from the characters of its own and Asparagaceae's by the rules at the flowering plants.
